hook: An empty hotel lobby full of things to find: tap each object in the picture, then give it its article.
intro: A picture hunt instead of a deck: one old-fashioned hotel lobby with 32 things to find in it, the words you need when you check in, wait for a room or ask at the desk — der Kronleuchter, die Tischklingel, das Gästebuch, der Gepäckwagen by the revolving door. The prompt asks, for example, Wo ist die Überwachungskamera? You tap it in the picture. Each find shows its label, coloured by its gender, then leaves a small tick in that colour, so you can see what you have already found. A tap on an empty spot costs nothing; a tap on the wrong object tells you what you hit and you keep looking, and after three misses the right one is shown. No object is asked twice in the same run. Once you have passed a run, the hunt turns harder: the prompt hides the article (Wo ist ___ Tischklingel?), and after the find you choose der, die or das yourself.
tips[0].title: Compounds in the hotel lobby: the last part decides
tips[0].text: Hotel words are almost all compounds, and only the last part decides the article. Schlüssel + Brett: das Brett, so das Schlüsselbrett. Tisch + Klingel: die Klingel, so die Tischklingel. Ignore the front part and look at the end.
tips[0].check.why: The last part is das Buch, so the whole word is das Gästebuch.
tips[1].title: Same front part, different article
tips[1].text: Two words can start the same way and still differ: das Klavier but die Klavierbank, die Blume but der Blumentopf. The front part never passes its article on, so learn each compound by its last part.
tips[1].check.why: The last part is der Topf, so it is der Blumentopf, even though die Blume comes first.
tips[2].title: Devices in -er are masculine
tips[2].text: A thing that does a job and ends in -er is nearly always der: der Feuerlöscher, der Wasserspender, der Kronleuchter, der Schirmständer. Picture a porter in the lobby holding each one, and the der sticks.
tips[2].check.why: Der Leuchter is a device ending in -er, so the compound is der Kronleuchter.
remember[0]: The last part of a compound sets the article: die Tischklingel because of die Klingel.
remember[1]: -er devices are der: der Feuerlöscher, der Wasserspender, der Kronleuchter.
remember[2]: Same start, new article: das Klavier but die Klavierbank.
